chunks: From him, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Hashimi, from Salih ibn Abi Hamad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ziyad ibn Salamah, who said:

I entered upon Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), and he said to me, 'O Ziyad, indeed you perform the work of the ruler.' I said, 'Yes.' He said to me, 'And why?' I said, 'I am a man who has dignity and dependents upon me, and there is nothing behind my back (no other source of support).'

He said to me, 'O Ziyad, for me to fall from a high place and be torn apart piece by piece is more beloved to me than that I hold a position of authority over any of them, or tread upon the carpet of any of them, except for what is mentioned.' I said, 'I do not know.'"

He said, 'Except for relieving a distress of a believer, or freeing his ransom, or paying off his debt. O Ziyad, indeed the lightest thing Allah, Exalted and Glorious, does to one who holds authority over them is that a tent of fire is set up over him until Allah, Exalted and Glorious, finishes the reckoning of the creatures.'
O Ziyad, if you are given charge of any of their affairs, then do good to your brothers, one for one, and Allah is beyond that.'
O Ziyad, whichever man among you holds authority over any of them, then equalizes you and them, say to him, 'You are a pretender, a liar.'

O Ziyad, when you remember your power over the people, remember Allah's power over you tomorrow, and the passing away of what you brought to them from them, and the staying of what you left for them upon you.'

key_terms.عَمَلَ السُّلْطَانِ: work of the ruler / holding authority

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of holding political or administrative authority in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) addresses Ziyad ibn Salamah, highlighting the spiritual peril of assuming administrative authority (*siyasa*) without sufficient merit. The Imam warns that even minor officials face the 'tent of fire' until the Day of Judgment unless they use their power to relieve believers' burdens, emphasizing that temporary worldly dominance is fleeting compared to eternal divine accountability.
